citations.claim: NS (approach 0) turned green at step 127 with 0s all-red, violating 4s requirement
EW still yellow at step 126 with emergency active, only 1s before forced red
EW was green at step 125 before emergency, shows normal cycle interrupted

counterfactual.change: Removed the emergency event (events=[]); otherwise identical parameters and steps. Without emergency preemption the controller respects yellow and all-red timings and no violation occurs, proving the emergency preemption bypass causes the failure.

explanation: Emergency preemption immediately forces direction switch without enforcing all-red clearance or yellow duration. At step 125 EW is green, at step 126 emergency on N becomes active and EW is forced to yellow, then at step 127 NS is forced to green after only 1s of yellow (need 6s) and 0s of all-red (need 4s). Removing the emergency eliminates the violation, confirming emergency handling bypasses clearance timing.

violation.detail: approach 0 turned green after only 0 s of all-red (need 4 s)

vision_note: At step 125 east-west has green while north-south is red, but at step 126 east-west is suddenly yellow and at step 127 north-south is already green while east-west is red. The direction switch occurs in only one second with no all-red clearance and with a truncated yellow.
